hypotheses.construction_plan: Instantiate the binary function template K(u, v) at (u, v) = (n, m) to produce the off-diagonal member; specialize v to u with u = n to produce the diagonal member.
required_assumptions: K is a binary function symbol
The diagonal assignment v = u is a valid specialization
proof_obligations: K(n, m) - K(u, v).subs({u: n, v: m}) = 0
K(n, n) - K(u, v).subs({u: n, v: n}) = 0
hypotheses.rationale: Both non-identical terms are evaluations of the same binary kernel K, with the second being the diagonal specialization of the first.

hypotheses.construction_plan: Use a conditional two-parameter template that selects K(u, v) when u != v and K(u, u) otherwise. Instantiating (u, v) = (n, m) gives the full piecewise expression; the branch values are the off-diagonal and diagonal cases of the template.
required_assumptions: The piecewise condition Ne(u, v) selects the second branch exactly when u == v
proof_obligations: Piecewise((K(n, m), Ne(n, m)), (K(n, n), True)) - Piecewise((K(u, v), Ne(u, v)), (K(u, u), True)).subs({u: n, v: m}) = 0
Under Ne(n, m), K(n, m) - K(u, v).subs({u: n, v: m}) = 0
Under not Ne(n, m), K(n, n) - K(u, u).subs({u: n}) = 0
hypotheses.rationale: The full expression is a conditional split of a single two-parameter kernel into off-diagonal and diagonal branches, so the piecewise template captures the shared branch structure.
